Subject: Burst policy simulations + NetOps handshake for Dedicated GPU pool

Team —

Quick note before I loop in StellarData: we need to run two final burst simulations (steady-state + holiday peak) against the proposed pool topology and autoscale policy so NetOps can validate egress, IP allowlists, and outage scenarios. Key asks:

- Monica: can you confirm the reserved pool size baseline (we discussed 8 A100-equivalent nodes) and whether customer wants burst capacity in the same region or cross-region fallback?
- Karthik: please run the simulation with these three policies: conservative (min instances 4 / max 12 / cooldown 120s), aggressive (min 4 / max 24 / cooldown 60s), and tiered (min 6 / max 16 with prewarm windows). Attach burst_sim_seed.json with traffic profile.
- Marissa: I'll draft the external intro once we have the first sim pass — include the onboarding_checklist_v2.pdf.

Deliverable: share sim results + a short table of expected 95th percentile p99 token latencies and cost delta for the three policies so Stellar's SRE can sign off.

Attachments: burst_sim_seed.json (configuration)

Rafael Mendes

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick context from our side:
- Production traffic today: sustained 800 requests/minute, typical sequence length ~220 tokens, peaking up to ~3,500 req/min during campaign windows (6–8 hours).
- Our compliance team requires that all egress endpoints be listed (we'll provide a CIDR block) and traffic over weekends gets routed through a different proxy — want to ensure prewarm works across those windows.
- We want to avoid cross-region fallback unless absolutely necessary due to PII processing rules. Prefer single-region w/ regional burst.

I'll share an aggregated traffic export and our CIDR allowlist by EOD Wednesday. Also looping Amit from VendorCloud — they manage our peering and will need the final IP ranges prior to cutover.

Regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Platform Reliability, StellarData
sarah.jenkins@stellardata.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@stellardata.com>, StellarData SRE <ops@stellardata.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Burst policy simulations + NetOps handshake for Dedicated GPU pool

Thanks, Sarah — that's helpful. A few technical clarifications and the first-pass results (summary):

Quoted for context:
> Marissa: I'll draft the external intro once we have the first sim pass — include the onboarding_checklist_v2.pdf.

Simulation notes (attached in Drive link):
- Traffic model used: sustained 800 rpm + 6-hour campaign peaking to 3.5k rpm, sequence len distribution centered at 220 tokens.
- Conservative policy (min 4 / max 12 / cooldown 120s): p95 latency 210ms, p99 410ms under peak; estimated token-cost delta +12% vs baseline.
- Aggressive policy (min 4 / max 24 / cooldown 60s): p95 160ms, p99 300ms; cost delta +28%.
- Tiered policy (prewarm windows for campaign hours; min 6 / max 16): p95 170ms, p99 320ms; cost delta +18%, but much smoother tail behavior during campaign ramp-ups.

NetOps asks for final handoff:
1) CIDR allowlist and any proxy egress IPs (we'll consume netops_ip_allowlist.txt).
2) VPN/peering window and primary contact (Amit?) for route validation.
3) SLA expectations for failover — confirm whether you want automatic cross-region fallback or manual failover.

Recommendation: start with the Tiered policy (best tradeoff of tail latency vs cost) with a 15-minute prewarm ahead of known campaign windows. If strict single-region processing is required, we'll size the regional pool with a slightly higher baseline (min 6 -> min 8) to reduce the need for cross-region fallback.

I'll prep pool_config_v1.xlsx with instance types, expected node counts, and the autoscale knobs. Rafael / Monica — let me know if you want me to include warm-cache preloads or KV cache priming in the sim (adds ~5–8% cost but reduces p99 substantially).

—Karthik
Principal SWEng, Inference Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
